name: historical_resolvability_blind_to_deleted_object
boundary: store.Has answers `held` for an object whose bytes are gone but whose index line survives, and checkpoint finalize decides pointer resolvability with it
seed_method: a real session through the installed binary, then one object file deleted from objects/ with index/roots.jsonl untouched; store.Has and an on-disk Lstat are then asked the same question
reason: the predicate internal/checkpoint decides pointer resolvability with agrees with the filesystem about a deleted object, and so does the root-level form of it. store.Has still answers from the index, which is its documented contract and no longer what a durable promise is made on.
detail: after deleting the object backing chunk 6139dde14f6a with its index line intact: store.Has(chunk)=true (the index's belief), store.ObjectOnDisk(chunk)=false (offered=true, the predicate the checkpoint decides with), the bytes are on disk=false, and the whole root 91daa03aa2e6 answers resolvable=false
